The study an instrument serves

Source: R/study.R
sframe_get_study.Rd

Returns the instrument's study: the problem statement, the objectives (each with an id such as "O1" and its text), and the sampling plan (population, method from sframe_sampling_methods(), method_other describing an "other" method, and planned_n). Set it with sframe_instrument(study = ) or by assigning instrument$study. Each plan block may name the objective it serves in its objective field. The study is never shown to respondents, since telling them the aims can bias their answers.

Usage

sframe_get_study(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An sframe object.

...

Ignored.

Value

A list with problem, objectives and sampling, each NULL when not declared.

Details

validate_sframe() refuses a malformed study, an objective id used twice and a plan block naming an objective that does not exist. It notes, without failing, an objective no research question serves, a research question that names no objective, and a problem statement over 150 words.

See also

Other Design functions: as_sframe(), launch_builder(), read_sframe(), sframe_attention_check(), sframe_branch(), sframe_choice_set(), sframe_conjoint_design(), sframe_instrument(), sframe_item(), sframe_sampling_methods(), sframe_scale(), sframe_validation, validate_sframe(), write_sframe()

Examples

ins <- sframe_instrument("Study", components = list(sframe_item("q1", "Q?", "text")),
  study = list(problem = "Why do students leave the course?",
               objectives = list(list(id = "O1", text = "Describe the reasons."))))
sframe_get_study(ins)$objectives
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$id
#> [1] "O1"
#> 
#> [[1]]$text
#> [1] "Describe the reasons."
#> 
#>
